name: Rumor Detection Benchmarks
description: New events emerge over time influencing the topics of rumors in social media. Current rumor detection benchmarks use random splits as training, development and test sets which typically results in topical overlaps. Consequently, models trained on random splits may not perform well on rumor classification on previously unseen topics due to the temporal concept drift. In this paper, we provide a re-evaluation of classification models on four popular rumor detection benchmarks considering chronological instead of random splits. Our experimental results show that the use of random splits can significantly overestimate predictive performance across all datasets and models. Therefore, we suggest that rumor detection models should always be evaluated using chronological splits for minimizing topical overlaps.
reputation: A well-studied rumor detection setting in social media NLP, but the paper mainly re-evaluates existing benchmarks under more realistic chronological splits rather than introducing a new widely used benchmark.
notes: Chronological splits are important because random splits can substantially overestimate performance due to topical overlap and temporal concept drift.
